summary: One machine with 200GB of room, six hours into a Booking, and a Run arrives asking for 900GB. The answer is the one an idle fleet gives: no machine here can hold it, so it waits for capacity to be added and the record projects no wait at all. What it must not be is refused. A projected wait was taken off every candidate whose Rental held a Booking, feasible or not, so this Run inherited the six hours somebody else declared as a max runtime, its class's four hour deadline was already inside that, and admission closed it as DEADLINE_UNREACHABLE at its very first pass having queued it for zero seconds. The identical submission against the identical idle machine was queued and kept for four hours, so whether a Run was told its deadline could not be met turned on whether an unrelated Run happened to be on a machine that could never take it either way. A wait nobody measured and a wait of zero are different facts, and the deadline rule refuses to guess over the difference: the projection now comes only from machines that could hold this Run once the capacity they are spending comes back, and none of these could.
